evidence: Contents lists "List of Figures . . . iv" but no corresponding "List of Tables" entry, despite the book containing numbered tables (1-1, 2-1, 2-2, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3, 4-1, 4-2, 5-1, 5-2, 6-1, 7-1, 7-2, 7-3, and at least 8-1).
issue: Navigation defect: the front matter provides a List of Figures but omits a List of Tables entirely, making the ~15 numbered tables undiscoverable from the front matter.
fix_instruction: Add a "List of Tables" to the front matter (after the List of Figures) enumerating every numbered table with its page number, or explicitly state why no List of Tables is provided.

evidence: Table 7-2 caption: "Table 7-2 — Memory floors by regime: inference and fine-tuning variants for the canonical 80-layer, hidden-8192, full-MHA 70B reference model." Rows give ~164.1 GB, ~152 GB, ~1,120 GB, ~280 GB, ~36 GB with no provenance/epistemic labels in any row and no table-level label convention stated.
issue: Evidence-label defect: Table 7-2 presents load-bearing quantitative values with no [canonical scenario]/[DERIVED]/[ASSUMPTION] labels. The Preface states a claim must carry labels inline or via an identified table/section that states them for every row; this table does neither, unlike Table 4-2 (Status column) and Table 7-1 (per-row labels).
fix_instruction: Add a provenance/status column or a table-level label note to Table 7-2 (e.g. [canonical scenario][DERIVED] for the 70B arithmetic rows, [1P][FACT] for the FP16/IEEE constants), consistent with Table 7-1 and Table 4-2.

evidence: Table 4-1, Economic constraints cell: "Infrastructure: ≈ $20/hour for an 8×H100 host at $2.50/GPU-hr on-demand [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]; not illustrative 2026 cloud-price input ($2.50/H100-GPU-hour, [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], not a market fact) → $20/hr per 8-GPU node"
issue: Prose defect: the clause "not illustrative 2026 cloud-price input" does not parse — it appears to be a merged/botched revision of "an illustrative 2026 cloud-price input" and "not a market fact", producing a self-contradictory fragment inside a dense table cell.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the clause to read, e.g., "an illustrative 2026 cloud-price input ($2.50/H100-GPU-hour, [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], not a market fact) → $20/hr per 8-GPU node".

evidence: "For the working method, begin at Ch. 1 (The Token) and follow the canonical workload through Chs. 16–17 and 20–21"
issue: Referent defect: "Ch. 1 (The Token)" conflates Chapter 1 with Part I. Chapter 1 is titled "It All Starts With the First Token"; "The Token" is the Part I divider title. A reader following this instruction may look for a chapter titled "The Token".
fix_instruction: Change to "begin at Ch. 1 ('It All Starts With the First Token', Part I)" or "begin with Part I (The Token), starting at Ch. 1".

evidence: "[HYPOTHESIS] : guardrail latency (PII redaction, refusal checking) on generated 300‑token outputs, ~2–8 ms/request on CPU in the illustrative scenario; measure on the target stack"
issue: Label-pair defect: this is a quantitative claim ("~2–8 ms/request") carrying only an Axis-2 tag ([HYPOTHESIS]) with no Axis-1 provenance tag, and it also calls itself "illustrative" without an [ILLUSTRATIVE] provenance tag. The Preface states a label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes.
fix_instruction: Tag the claim with a full pair, e.g. [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] (non-canonical worked figure, reasoned but unvalidated), and drop the redundant word "illustrative" from the sentence.

evidence: "A section reference takes the form § N.M, which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement), not Section 1's fourth subsection."
issue: Convention inconsistency: the Preface defines the form as "§ N.M" (with a space), but the body predominantly uses the no-space form ("§7.3", "§4.6", "§8.3.3", "§6.3.4") and occasionally the spaced form ("§ 7.3", "§ 1.4"). Both forms are in use across the book, so the stated convention does not match the actual style.
fix_instruction: Pick one form (recommend the no-space "§N.M" used by the majority of the body) and either normalize the whole book or state that the space is optional.

evidence: "a low-batch (single-stream) decode rate of ~50 tokens/s on 8×H100 with a 70B FP16 model and 9.2K context for 300‑token outputs. The prefill phase (9.2K tokens) dominates TTFT: at ~1.08 s it leaves ~0.12 s against the 1.2 s budget — exactly the ~120 ms retrieval allocation, i.e. zero true headroom."
issue: Prose ambiguity: "The prefill phase ... dominates TTFT" is immediately qualified by "at ~1.08 s it leaves ~0.12 s", but the sentence does not name the retrieval term as the subtracted quantity until the clause after the dash. A reader can momentarily read "1.08 s dominates TTFT" as a claim that prefill is the whole TTFT, contradicting the TTFTe2e formula (retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill) defined in Ch 2 and Ch 4.
fix_instruction: Rewrite as: "Within the 1.2 s TTFT budget, prefill is allocated ~1.08 s and retrieval ~120 ms, leaving zero true headroom on the two-term model (admission/queue and tokenization/transfer are outside it)."

evidence: Figure 7.5 caption: "FP16 bound reaches the 436 GB budget at ~166K" ... "the GQA FP16 line at 327,680 B/token reaches that budget only at ~1.33M tokens"
issue: Figure-vs-text unit inconsistency: the figure's vertical axis is labeled "KV cache size (GB)" and the caption says "The axis and every series are aggregate whole-host GB". The 436 GB budget is an aggregate whole-host figure. But the 9.5K GQA annotation "≈ 3.1 GB (GQA FP16)" is a per-rank value (24.9 ÷ 8), not an aggregate whole-host value — the caption admits this ("24.9 ÷ 8 ≈ 3.1 GB per rank at 9.5K, to be read against an 80 GB rank, not against the aggregate budget line"). Mixing per-rank and aggregate values on one aggregate axis is confusing.
fix_instruction: Move the per-rank 3.1 GB annotation off the aggregate axis, or relabel it explicitly as "per-rank" and draw it against a secondary per-rank axis; alternatively, plot the aggregate GQA value (~24.9 GB at 9.5K) on the aggregate axis.
